newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans lower on weather, July liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans lower on weather, July liquidation.

text.p: CBOT soybeans were lower at midsession Wednesday on favorable crop weather, and July was sharply lower on liquidation before first notice day Monday, traders said.
"We're just seeing continued liquidation in July," said one floor trader.
One analyst said that interest in July was waning because tight supplies have left that contract vulnerable to wide price swings, especially after first notice day Monday.
"Remember we're taking the limit off July on Monday," said the analyst.
Good growing weather was reported throughout most of the U.S. Midwest. Many areas have received timely rains, and most have high temperatures in the 80s and 90s Fahrenheit.
July also labored under pressure from talk that one large commercial firm was barging a rumored four cargos of beans to Chicago to deliver against the board.
In early trade, Lind-Waldock sold three million bushels November, Rosenthal Collins sold one million November and Refco bought one million November.
At 1113 CDT, July soybeans were eleven cents lower at $8.20 per bushel, and other months were 3/4 to 6-1/2 lower.
Traders are also beginning to square positions before the U.S. Department of Agriculutre's acreage and quarterly stocks forecasts on Monday.
Analysts' estimates for the USDA acreage forecast ranged from 67.3 to 69.5 million acres. Analysts' estimates for quarterly stocks ranged from 499 million to 537 million bushels.

On the day, Merrill Lynch bought two million bushels November, L.B. Stern bought two million November and Cargill Investor Services bought 2.5 million July. Iowa Grain sold three million bushels July and Lind-Waldock sold three million November.
In options trade, Tenco bought 400 August $7.25 calls and ADM sold 300 September $8.00 calls, pit traders siad.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 63,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 59,930 contracts.
